label: rem:phi-n-global-section
title: $\Phi_n$ as the global section of the categorical mass functor
html:
Remark. \Phi_n as the global section of the categorical mass functor

In the algebraic refactor of the magic-number / shell-closure framework, the categorical mass endomorphism \Phi_n acts globally, not locally. It is not built per-vortex and combined by tensor product. Instead \Phi_n forms the global section of the categorical mass functor over the rigid braided monoidal category \mathbf{C}, in the strict sense of monoidal-category global sections: \Phi_n \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^{\otimes n}) is determined by its compatibility with the Frobenius-Hopf substrate axioms across every sub-tensor-factor of A^{\otimes n}, not by an additive combination of local pieces.

Necessity of dropping locality

Local trivialisation—"screening"—provided the framework's earlier explanation of shell closure: that something local at each vortex trivialises the full-twist action. That picture carries two flaws:

  1. Anomalous ribbon flux. A non-trivial ribbon (= framing) action on \Phi_n at a non-magic level n would propagate unboundedly up the brane tower (recursive-brane-tower). Each brane level A_{n+1} = A_n \otimes \Omega^1(A_n) inherits the framing flux. Without a global cancellation mechanism, the accumulated flux at the descent limit diverges.
  2. Finite observable mass. The categorical mass identity (def:hecke-mass-element) is finite: \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) \in \mathbb{R} for every observed hadron. Finite observable mass remains incompatible with unbounded framing flux.

The only consistent reconciliation requires global topological neutrality at saturation: at n \in \mathfrak{M}, the ribbon action on \Phi_n evaluates globally to zero (in the centre-of-the-braid-group sense), not locally trivialised by some spectator structure. This forms precisely the prop:categorical-neutrality-saturated-shells statement. It provides the structural reason a non-trivial action cannot coexist with finite mass at saturated n.

The categorical-functor view

In the language of monoidal functors, \Phi_n is

  \Phi_n = (\text{global section of } \mathcal{F}_{\text{mass}})_n,
\qquad
  \mathcal{F}_{\text{mass}}:
    \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{C},
\qquad
  X \mapsto (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ (X \otimes -).

The functor \mathcal{F}_{\text{mass}} takes a substrate object X to its mass endomorphism. The global section \Phi_n at level n provides the assignment of \mathcal{F}_{\text{mass}}(A^{\otimes n}) that respects all the substrate's monoidal-functor structure simultaneously—including the central full-twist action on each A^{\otimes n}. Demanding that \Phi_n form a single global section, rather than a colimit of local pieces, enforces the substrate-level constraint that the central action vanishes at saturated n.

Implications for the conjecture

conj:mass-endomorphism (the open problem of finding a closed-form NF for \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}) is correspondingly reframed. The conjecture is no longer "find the local NF generators and combine". It becomes "find the categorical global section that satisfies the saturated-shell global-neutrality constraint". The reframing constructs the magic-number ladder as a structural prediction rather than a numerical phenomenon.

This remark interprets conj:mass-endomorphism only. It makes no new logical claim. The mathematical content resides in the saturated-shell and shell-condensation conjectures, which are themselves conditional on the algebraic refactor.
